gaps: No alerting on repeated 500 responses from the application tier
Administrative console logins are not forwarded to the SIEM

findings.title: SQL Injection in login form (uid parameter)
findings.description: The uid parameter of the login form is concatenated directly into a SQL statement. A single-quote payload produces a database error, and boolean-based conditions alter the authentication outcome, confirming that input is parsed as SQL.
findings.evidence: POST /bank/login.jsp uid=admin'--&passw=x -> HTTP 302 to /bank/main.jsp (authenticated session established without a valid password). Control request uid=admin&passw=x -> HTTP 200 with 'Login Failed'.

findings.title: Default administrative credentials accepted on /admin
findings.description: The administrative interface authenticates the shipped default account. No multi-factor challenge is presented and the interface is reachable from the public internet.
findings.evidence: GET /admin/ -> 401; POST /admin/j_security_check with admin:admin -> 302 to /admin/dashboard.jsp with JSESSIONID issued.

findings.title: Apache Tomcat 8.5.31 — multiple known vulnerabilities
findings.description: The server banner and error pages identify Apache Tomcat 8.5.31, which is past end of support and affected by publicly documented vulnerabilities including the Ghostcat AJP file read issue.
findings.evidence: Server: Apache-Coyote/1.1; 404 page footer reports 'Apache Tomcat/8.5.31'.

findings.title: Reflected Cross-Site Scripting in search parameter
findings.description: The query parameter is reflected into the response body without contextual output encoding, allowing script execution in the context of the application origin.
findings.evidence: GET /search.jsp?query=<script>alert(1)</script> -> the payload appears unencoded inside the results heading element.

findings.title: Missing security response headers
findings.description: Responses omit Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options and Strict-Transport-Security.
findings.evidence: HEAD / -> response headers: Server, Date, Content-Type, Set-Cookie. None of the expected security headers are present.

steps: Bypass authentication via SQL injection in uid
Access authenticated banking session and customer records
attack_paths.terminal_impact: Unauthorised access to customer financial records

gaps: Application error responses are not monitored
No WAF in front of the application tier
